correctness.rationale: Exact boundary edges are n before the bridge, giving the birthday product; after the bridge, every unvisited peripheral has symmetric and independently resolved competing parent edges. The resulting mixture yields exact moments. A conditional characteristic-function calculation proves independent Gaussian noise and the Rayleigh limit; bounded birthday tails justify moment convergence. A coupling of identical fair-parent coins proves all-n stochastic dominance. An independent Markov-chain enumeration checks n=1..8 and 2541 assertions; computation is corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The degree law quantifies a nontrivial first-passage growth bias on a natural two-hub network: root degree shifts by order sqrt(n), acquires a non-Gaussian limit, and strictly dominates the root degree of the uniform spanning tree. It distinguishes network growth mechanisms by a structural statistic not given by height bounds, a random-tree count or the classical birthday collision law alone.
